reasons: Lake verifies United States v. Sokolow, U.S. Supreme Court, 1989, official citation 490 U.S. 1.
Pinpoint pin-9 supports the table proposition that individually innocent factors can amount to reasonable suspicion when taken together.
Lake verifies United States v. Brignoni-Ponce, U.S. Supreme Court, 1975, official citation 422 U.S. 873.
Lake pinpoints describe the roving-patrol stop rule and the insufficiency of apparent Mexican ancestry standing alone.
Lake verifies Michigan v. Long, U.S. Supreme Court, 1983, official citation 463 U.S. 1032.
Lake pinpoint pin-1049 identifies the Terry protective-search rationale for a passenger-compartment weapons search during an investigative stop.
Lake verifies Delaware v. Prouse, U.S. Supreme Court, 1979, official citation 440 U.S. 648.
Lake pinpoint pin-663 describes the issue as a stop without articulable and reasonable suspicion and the rule as no.
Lake verifies Terry v. Ohio, U.S. Supreme Court, 1968, official citation 392 U.S. 1.
Lake treatment calls Terry the foundational stop-and-frisk authority, and pinpoints support a limited stop and frisk based on specific circumstances rather than a hunch.
Lake verifies Maryland v. Buie, U.S. Supreme Court, 1990, official citation 494 U.S. 325.
Star-verified pin-335 supports the articulable-facts rule for a sweep where the area harbors a dangerous person.
Lake verifies United States v. Cortez, U.S. Supreme Court, 1981, official citation 449 U.S. 411.
Lake treatment expressly identifies the 'particularized and objective basis' and 'whole picture' formulation of reasonable suspicion.
Lake verifies Kansas v. Glover, U.S. Supreme Court, 2020, official citation 589 U.S. 376.
Lake treatment and star-verified pin-1188 support the registered-owner revoked-license inference, cabined by facts negating the inference.
Lake verifies Illinois v. Wardlow, U.S. Supreme Court, 2000, official citation 528 U.S. 119.
Star-verified pin-124a supports the headlong-flight proposition in the context of a high-crime area.
Lake verifies Adams v. Williams, U.S. Supreme Court, 1972, official citation 407 U.S. 143.
Lake treatment states that a known, face-to-face informant's tip carries enough reliability for a Terry stop and protective frisk.

defect.problem: The case and citation stand, but the table's opinion link does not match the disclosed lake record URL.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the opinion link to the lake record URL /opinion/9189388/florida-v-j-l/.

reasons: Lake verifies Florida v. J. L., U.S. Supreme Court, 2000, official citation 529 U.S. 266.
Lake pinpoint pin-272 supports the bare anonymous gun-tip rule, but the payload link points to /opinion/118352/florida-v-jl/ rather than the lake absolute_url.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the lake canonical caption spacing if exact-caption normalization matters: Florida v. J. L.

reasons: Lake verifies United States v. Hensley, U.S. Supreme Court, 1985, official citation 469 U.S. 221.
Lake pin-233 supports reliance on a flyer or bulletin if the issuing police possessed reasonable suspicion justifying the stop.
Lake verifies United States v. Arvizu, U.S. Supreme Court, 2002, official citation 534 U.S. 266.
Lake treatment and pin-274 support totality review and reject divide-and-conquer analysis.

defect.problem: The cited official reporter citation 574 U.S. 54 is not verifiable from the disclosed Heien lake record; the record has official/display citation null, expected_citation_found false, and status under_review.
defect.proposed_fix: Use a citation present in the lake record, such as 135 S. Ct. 530, or supply/update the lake record with verified support for 574 U.S. 54.

reasons: Lake identity verifies the case name, court, year, and URL, but not the asserted U.S. reporter citation.
Because citation exactness is part of the existence assertion, the assertion cannot stand from disclosed evidence.
residual_risks: The 574 U.S. citation may be correct outside the disclosed record, but the ground rules do not allow relying on outside knowledge.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid official U.S. reporter citations that the lake record does not itself verify.

reasons: Lake verifies Alabama v. White, U.S. Supreme Court, 1990, official citation 496 U.S. 325.
Lake pin-332 and pin-332a support corroborated prediction of future conduct as supplying reasonable suspicion in a close case.
Lake verifies the Navarette record as U.S. Supreme Court, 2014, and citations.all includes 572 U.S. 393.
Lake treatment and pin-398 support that an adequately reliable 911 dangerous-driving tip may supply reasonable suspicion.
residual_risks: Lake captions the case Prado Navarette v. California and has official/display citation null despite listing 572 U.S. 393 in citations.all.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If strict canonical captioning is required, use Prado Navarette v. California.

defect.evidence_quote: the issue is whether a reasonably prudent man in the circumstances would be warranted in the belief that his safety or that of others was in danger.
defect.problem: The black-letter rule relies on verbatim Terry and Cortez quotations and pincites that are not verifiable from disclosed text; Terry pin-27 lands on different text, and no text/Terry or text/Cortez opinion file is present. The opening sentence also risks implying that reasonable suspicion of crime alone justifies a frisk, while Terry pin-30 requires danger/weapon facts.
defect.proposed_fix: Add verified opinion text or lake pinpoints for the quoted Terry and Cortez language, correct the pincites, and qualify the frisk rule to require reasonable suspicion that the person is armed and dangerous.

reasons: The quoted Terry language does not appear in the disclosed Terry pinpoints, and pin-27's star-verified quote is a different safety-danger sentence.
Cortez treatment supports the general formulation, but the disclosed Cortez pinpoint is slip-only and does not provide character-faithful quote verification for the quoted phrase at 417-18.
Terry pin-30 supports a frisk only where criminal activity may be afoot and the person may be armed and presently dangerous.
residual_risks: The rule may be accurate in outside law, but the required quote-fidelity and pincite support are not disclosed here.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: State: reasonable suspicion supports a brief investigative stop; a protective frisk requires reasonable suspicion that the person is armed and dangerous.
